newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PNB unveils benefits of PNB-Republic sale.
newsitem.headline: PNB unveils benefits of PNB-Republic sale.

text.p: Philippine National Bank (PNB) said on Thursday net proceeds from the 60 percent sale of its subsidiary PNB-Republic Bank would mainly go to building its reserves.
PNB recently sold 60 percent of PNB-Republic to Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) for 880 million pesos.
"Any windfall coming from the sale of PNB-Republic will be put in reserves," senior vice-president Valentin Araneta told analysts at a briefing.
The bank is putting aside substantial reserves to cover its past due accounts, which stood at four percent of its outstanding loan portfolio as of the first quarter of the year.
Of the total proceeds from the sale, PNB will remit 150 million pesos to an escrow account to settle the outstanding liabilities of PNB-Republic to the Philippine central bank.
Besides the central bank's liabilities, PNB will also assume 1.8 billion pesos worth of assets and some bad debts amounting to 300 million pesos, senior vice-president Emerita Diaz said.
Most of the bad debts were fully collateralised, she said.
The rest of the loan portfolio includes government securities and two major loan accounts.
"What we will be getting is 40 percent of a bank with a clean balance sheet and a strong partner," Araneta said of the sale.
